Soundboard Engine

A shared C++17 DJ audio engine with no dependencies and a plain C API (include/soundboard/sbe.h) for Swift and JNI.

Features

  • 1–4 decks: Hermite-interpolated variable-rate playback, CDJ-style cue, 8 hot cues, beat loops, beat jump, nudge, quantise. Every transport action is declicked.
  • Mixer: trim and auto-gain, Linkwitz–Riley 3-band isolator EQ with kill, bipolar SVF filter, fader, beat-synced echo, constant-power and cut crossfader curves.
  • Buses: master with a look-ahead limiter and record tap. Headphone cue with PFL, cue/master blend, its own gain and a safety limiter. Library preview into the headphones only.
  • Routing: master-only, split-mono, multichannel, and a separate cue device (with drift compensation). Per-bus latency compensation.
  • Sync: tempo + phase match with a PLL lock, half/double-time aware.
  • Transitions: blend, bass swap, filter sweep, echo out — all beat-length.
  • Analysis: BPM + beat grid, key (Camelot), BS.1770 loudness, 3-band waveform.

Layout

include/soundboard/sbe.h   C API (the only header hosts need)
src/                       engine, deck, DSP, FIFOs, analysis, WAV I/O
tests/test_main.cpp        25 tests, dependency-free
testing/synth.hpp          deterministic synthetic tracks for tests and the prototype
tools/routing_demo.cpp     offline routing prototype

Run

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j
./build/sbe_tests                 # optional filter: ./build/sbe_tests sync
./build/sbe_routing_demo /tmp     # or: ./build/sbe_routing_demo /tmp a.wav b.wav

Real-time rules on the audio thread: no locks, no allocation, no frees, no I/O. All control calls travel over a lock-free SPSC queue, and track memory is released only after the audio thread acknowledges the swap.

Source: engine/README.md
